top_choice_rationale: P002 (Melitz and Helpman, firm heterogeneity and selection in trade) is my first choice on achievement, maturity, attribution and citation scope. Melitz (2003) is a single originating contribution, and Helpman's work, including Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exporting versus FDI, made it a general research programme. The selection and reallocation mechanism has been tested on firm-level and transaction-level data for over twenty years without its core being overturned. It now underlies work on productivity, reallocation and policy evaluation. The two-name credit is tight, provided the citation rests on the selection and reallocation mechanism and does not claim the Bernard-Jensen or Eaton-Kortum contributions or specific welfare magnitudes, which depend on functional form. P001 (Autor, Dorn and Hanson) is a strong second. It has credible designs and a first-order question, and its three-name credit is clean if the citation is worded around the empirical evidence. I rank it below P002 because the size and persistence of the effects are still being revised and the task framework has originators outside the credited set. It is nevertheless clearly preferable to no award. P000 is last because two well-attributed, prize-level proposals are available.
recusal_note: I co-authored a 2026 IJIO paper with committee chair John Hassler and former chair Tore Ellingsen. Hassler also supports P002, so I do not treat his agreement as independent evidence of merit. I am married to Magdalena Andersson, a public fact that is not linked to any committee colleague or candidate. No collaboration or institutional tie to Melitz, Helpman, Autor, Dorn or Hanson is apparent from my profile. My fields (industrial organisation, trade, pricing) are adjacent to P002, which I treat as expertise and not as evidence of merit. These are disclosed, not adjudicated.
